verification.note: ESA report dated Sept. 14 (based on end-2025 data) supports >300 launches/>4,000 payloads, >3 intact objects reentering daily, runaway LEO objects/collisions despite 100-year horizon, and active debris removal required.

claim: NASA's Moon Base program manager said on 15 September 2026 that only one of the four lunar landers planned for 2026 (Astrobotic's Griffin, no earlier than November) is still expected to launch this year: Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance (delayed by a May New Glenn pad explosion) and Intuitive Machines' Nova-C Trinity slipped to the first part of 2027 and Firefly's Blue Ghost 2 to later in 2027.

sources.title: NASA expects one lunar launch this year, Moon Base manager says (Aerospace America)

verification.note: Aerospace America’s Sep. 15 report says Griffin is no earlier than November, while Mark 1 Endurance and Nova-C Trinity move to the first part of 2027 and Blue Ghost 2 later in 2027; it attributes the Mark 1 delay to the May New Glenn pad explosion. All details supported.

claim: At China's first Space Medical Engineering Conference (19–20 September 2026), attendees were told that Tiangong's regenerative life support system had operated in orbit for more than five years with 100% oxygen closure and over 96% water closure.

sources.title: 望宇登月服研制进展顺利 (People's Daily, 22 Sep 2026)

verification.note: People's Daily says the Sept. 19–20 conference was told the system had operated more than five years, with 100% oxygen and over 96% water closure. It does not support the comparison to a 2023 figure; removed that detail.

claim: The Astronaut Center of China said on 21 September 2026 that more than 20 varieties of 14 plant species have been cultivated aboard the Tiangong space station, with wheat completing a full growing cycle and a second crop from those seeds close to harvest, as groundwork for station crop production and a planned "lunar vegetable garden".

sources.title: China cultivates 14 plant species aboard space station (Xinhua)

verification.note: Xinhua dated Sep. 21 reports more than 20 varieties across 14 species cultivated in orbit, wheat completed a full growing cycle, a second round using its seeds is close to reaping, and China intends a “lunar vegetable garden.” The achievement and attribution are supported.

claim: The UN COPUOS Legal Subcommittee's Working Group on Legal Aspects of Space Resource Activities circulated, with its 24 September 2026 intersessional meeting, a consolidated draft of non-binding Initial Recommended Principles for Space Resource Activities stating that extraction of space resources in compliance with the Outer Space Treaty 'does not inherently constitute national appropriation', for negotiation toward the April 2027 Legal Subcommittee session.

sources.title: Consolidated draft set of Initial Recommended Principles for Space Resource Activities (UNOOSA)
Space Resources and the Anatomy of Consensus at COPUOS (Opinio Juris, 25 Sep 2026)

verification.note: UNOOSA draft and September 25 analysis confirm the circulated non-binding draft, the quoted non-appropriation formulation, and negotiation toward the April 2027 session. Opinio Juris dates circulation in conjunction with the September 24 intersessional meeting; published date September 25 is supported.

claim: NASA named five winners (113 submissions from 33 countries) of its Deep Space Food Challenge: Mars to Table on 24 September 2026, awarding $650,000 in total for paper concepts of food systems for a 15-person crew over 500 sols on Mars; the $300,000 first prize went to the ANI concept, which combines crops, fermentation, fungi and bioreactor nutrient recycling to produce 50% of the food away from Earth.

sources.title: NASA Unveils Winning Designs for Mars Space Food Systems Challenge (24 Sep 2026)
NASA Back for Seconds with New Food System Design Challenge (13 Jan 2026)

verification.note: NASA reports five winners among 113 submissions from 33 countries and $650,000 total awards; mission scenario is 15 people for 500 Martian sols. ANI won $300,000 and combines crops, fermentation/fungi, bioreactor nutrient recycling, and aims to produce 50% of food away from Earth. Published Sept. 24.

claim: With Albania, Croatia, Côte d’Ivoire and San Marino signing, the Artemis Accords reached 76 signatory countries by 28 September 2026.

sources.title: NASA Celebrates as Artemis Accords Surpasses 75 Signatories

verification.note: NASA’s Sep. 28 release names Albania, Croatia, Côte d’Ivoire and San Marino and says their participation brings the total to 76 countries. The cited release does not substantiate the comparison with 59 in October 2025, so removed it.

claim: NASA said on 28 September 2026 that Boeing's uncrewed Starliner-1 engineering-evaluation mission could fly in December 2026 or January 2027 and that it plans to return astronauts on Starliner-2 by 2028.

sources.title: NASA, Boeing Share Update on Commercial Starliner Development Plans (NASA)

verification.note: NASA release dated Sept. 28 says Starliner-1 could fly in December or January 2027 as an engineering evaluation and states plan to return astronauts on Starliner-2 by 2028. Kind setback fits program delay context.

claim: Starship Flight 14 on 28 September 2026 became the first Starship to reach Earth orbit and its first to deliver meaningful payload there, deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites before performing its first deorbit burn and splashing down on target in the northern Pacific.

sources.title: SpaceX: Starship Flight 14
SpaceX update: Starship to Orbit (15 Sep 2026)

verification.note: SpaceX Flight 14 page (September 28) explicitly calls it first orbital Starship flight and first meaningful payload delivery, confirms 26 Starlink V3 deployments, first deorbit burn and targeted Pacific splashdown; achievement/date match. Update page also cited.

claim: NASA selected three PRISM science payload suites for CLPS delivery under its Moon Base program on 30 September 2026, including DISCO (Ames, PI Ariel Deutsch), which is to make the first direct on-surface measurements of ice in lunar micro-cold traps, pinpointing where ice exists and how much to inform turning ice into a usable resource for Moon Base (no flight date given).

sources.title: NASA Adds New Science Investigations for Moon Base (NASA, 30 Sep 2026)

verification.note: NASA’s September 30 release reports selection of three PRISM suites, including DISCO (Ames; PI Ariel Deutsch), for first direct surface measurements of ice in micro-cold traps to locate and quantify ice for Moon Base planning; no flight date stated.

claim: Varda raised a $251 million Series D (total raised $598 million) on 30 September 2026 to scale toward the first pharmaceutical made in space for patients on Earth, having completed six successful reentry missions with over a dozen more launches and reentries planned through 2028.

sources.title: Varda press release: $251 Million Series D (30 Sep 2026)

verification.note: Varda's Sept. 30 release states $251 million Series D, $598 million total raised, six successful reentry missions and over a dozen more launches/reentries planned through 2028. It describes getting closer to delivering the first medicine made in space; date and announcement kind match.

claim: Varda launched its W-8 and W-9 reentry vehicles together on SpaceX's Transporter-18 on 1 October 2026, the first time two commercial reentry vehicles went to orbit at the same time; they carry thermal-protection payloads and, on W-9, a navigation system for hypersonic flight, for commercial and government customers.

sources.title: Varda press release: Varda Launches Two Vehicles to Orbit at the Same Time (1 Oct 2026)

verification.note: Varda release (1 Oct): W-8 and W-9 launched on Transporter-18, 'the first time in history that two commercial reentry vehicles will be sent to orbit at the same time'; W-8 carries thermal-protection sensing/materials payloads, W-9 a hypersonic-flight navigation system and heatshield materials, for commercial and government customers. Fixed the payload description (navigation only on W-9) and removed the unstated 'rather than pharmaceutical processing'.

claim: The U.S. DOT announced five proposed FAA rules to streamline Part 450 commercial launch and reentry licensing (electronic applications, more flexibility to show equivalent safety, combining three safety analyses into one submission), citing 217 of 329 commercial launches worldwide in 2025 by the U.S. and an expectation of 10,000 FAA-licensed launches and reentries a year by 2035.

sources.title: Trump's Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces Five Actions to Accelerate Commercial Space Licensing (USDOT)
DOT Proposes Changes to Part 450 Licensing Rules (Payload)

verification.note: USDOT release lists the five Part 450 NPRMs (electronic applications, flight-safety means of compliance etc.) and the 217 of 329 launches / 10,000 by 2035 figures; Payload (8 Oct) says Duffy announced them 'on Tuesday' (= 6 Oct). Published 2026-10-08 = Payload date (DOT page shows no print date).

claim: NASA’s Human Landing System paper for IAC 2026 (5–9 October) says the agency is working toward the Artemis IV crewed lunar landing in early 2028 and a second crewed landing, Artemis V, in late 2028; after Artemis III, SpaceX and Blue Origin are to demonstrate uncrewed precision lunar landings, with autonomous landing accuracy within 100 m of a target, and providers to be assigned to the crewed missions later.

sources.title: NASA's Human Landing System: Demonstrating the Capability to Land Artemis Astronauts on the Moon by 2028 (IAC 2026, NTRS)

verification.note: NTRS 20260008717 paper (NTRS distribution date 2026-10-09, IAC 5–9 Oct): 'the Artemis IV crewed lunar landing in early 2028 and a second crewed landing, Artemis V, in late 2028'; SpaceX and Blue Origin 'will demonstrate autonomous precision lunar landings' within 100 m; providers assigned to missions later. Reworded the demo-landing clause to match the paper; published stays 2026-10-09.

claim: NASA released its final Request for Proposals for commercial low Earth orbit space stations to follow the ISS on 9 October 2026, planning multi-award firm-fixed-price IDIQ contracts with proposals due 8 December 2026 and awards expected in spring 2027.

sources.title: NASA: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations (Oct 2026)

verification.note: NASA's Oct. 9 release says it released the final RFP; proposals due Dec. 8, awards expected spring 2027, and contracts are firm-fixed-price, multi-award IDIQ. Published date and government-action kind are consistent.

claim: NASA's Human Landing System presentation at IAC 2026 (5-9 October) schedules SpaceX's Starship ship-to-ship propellant transfer demo for Q1 2027, after a first ship catch and first Cape flight in Q4 2026, whereas SpaceX's October 2025 update had targeted the in-space propellant transfer flight test for 2026.

sources.title: NASA NTRS: NASA's Human Landing System - Demonstrating the Capability to Land Artemis Astronauts on the Moon by 2028 (IAC 2026 presentation)
SpaceX update: To the Moon and Beyond (30 Oct 2025)

verification.note: NTRS 20260009199 (IAC 2026 presentation, NTRS distribution date 2026-10-09) timeline chart: First Orbital Flight, v3 booster catch, First Ship Catch, First Cape Flight in Q4 2026, 'Prop Transfer Demo' in Q1 2027. SpaceX update 'To the Moon and Beyond' (2025-10-30): long-duration and in-space propellant transfer flight tests 'targeted to take place in 2026'.

claim: On 14 October 2026 the FAA announced its intent to prepare a Programmatic EIS on SpaceX’s proposal to raise Starship operations at Starbase from the currently authorized 25 launches and 50 landings per year to up to 100 launches and 200 landings a year in Phase 1 and up to 456 launches and 912 landings a year in Phase 2.

sources.title: Federal Register: Notice of Intent to Prepare a PEIS on SpaceX Starship-Super Heavy operations at Starbase (14 Oct 2026)
FAA: SpaceX Starship Super Heavy Project at the Boca Chica Launch Site

verification.note: Federal Register says FAA announced intent to prepare PEIS, not that it ‘will prepare’ as a completed action; current authorization is up to 25 launches and 50 total landings, not 25 launches alone. Proposed Phase 1/2 limits match. FAA notice gives exact Oct. 14 date.

claim: Rocket Lab said on 14 October 2026 that its medium-lift reusable Neutron will not fly until 2027 after voids were found in carbon-composite propellant-tank domes of the first stage, traced to a design change made after a tank ruptured in a hydrostatic test in January; Neutron was announced in 2021 for a 2024 first flight.

sources.title: Neutron's first launch slips again amid trouble with carbon composites (Ars Technica)

verification.note: Ars published Oct. 15: Rocket Lab announced Wednesday Neutron won’t fly until 2027; voids in first-stage tank domes trace to design change after January hydrostatic-test rupture. It confirms 2021 announcement targeting 2024.
